log: Extends the new base-unit-type-diplomatic instead of Fortifiable (civ-clone/web-renderer#34). Diplomatic extends Fortifiable, so it can still fortify.
Also the standard CI (civ-clone/web-renderer#66): the pnpm build workflow, prettier --check, and no yarn or npm lock file.
Extends the new base-unit-type-diplomatic instead of Fortifiable (civ-clone/web-renderer#34). Diplomatic extends Fortifiable, so it can still fortify.
Also the standard CI (civ-clone/web-renderer#66): the pnpm build workflow, prettier --check, and no yarn or npm lock file.

A Fortifiable type for non-military units (Diplomats and Caravans), so rules can exclude them from unit support, military unhappiness, zones of control, attacks and city capture (civ-clone/web-renderer#34).

v474.05 skips them in the city's unit support loop (OpenCivOne CityWorker.cs L422-L430), so they cost no shield under any government and don't take one of Anarchy's or Despotism's free units (civ-clone/web-renderer#34).

v474.05 (OpenCivOne CityWorker.cs L422-L460) counts a supported unit if its attack is non-zero and it is an aircraft (wherever it is) or away from the city, skipping Diplomats and Caravans. The rule counted every Air, Fortifiable and Naval unit away from the city, so an unarmed Transport, a Caravan or a Diplomat caused unhappiness, and a Bomber at home didn't (civ-clone/web-renderer#181, #34).
v474.05 lets Diplomats and Caravans pass enemy units, and stops them before any combat or capture (civ-clone/web-renderer#34):
move: restore the commented-out Diplomatic exemption from the adjacency rule;
attackCriteria and captureCityCriteria (attack, sneak-attack, capture-city, sneak-capture-city) exclude Diplomatic;
pillage tests for Diplomatic instead of naming Caravan and Diplomat.
test: no sneak attack or capture for Diplomatic units at peace either
Types/Diplomatic re-exports base-unit-type-diplomatic, the type Caravan and Diplomat now extend (civ-clone/web-renderer#34).
Mirrors civ1-city's support rules, which now skip Diplomatic units (civ-clone/web-renderer#34), so the AI doesn't think a city pays for them or that they use up a free unit.

Knowledge#unitSupport takes the unit type in question and returns 0 for a Diplomatic one, so buildItemInCity no longer filters Diplomats and Caravans out of a city that couldn't support another military unit, and takeUpStation lets one rehome there.
